title: The Price Effects of S&P 500 Index Changes: Is the Demand for Stocks Perfectly Elastic?
one_line: Additions to the S&P 500 earn a permanent price gain while deletions suffer only a temporary decline — an asymmetry explained by investor awareness (added stocks become better known; deleted ones don't become less known).

findings.statement: Permanent increase for additions, temporary decrease for deletions (1962-2000).

why.pattern: Investor recognition plus index-fund price pressure.

reported_results.headline: Additions to the S&P 500 earn a permanent price gain while deletions suffer only a temporary decline — an asymmetry explained by investor awareness (added stocks become better known; deleted ones don't become less known).
